label: Water Pump
description: Centrifugal water pump driven by an electric motor through a coupling.
general_safety: Isolate and lock out the driver and close the suction and discharge valves before opening the pump.
Depressurise and drain the casing before removing seals, plugs or covers; hot or pressurised water can cause burns.
Keep guards on the coupling and never touch it while the pump is running.
general_inspection: Check suction and discharge pressure, flow and motor current against the pump curve or nameplate.
Check visually for leaks, loose bolts, coupling condition and pipe strain.
Confirm the pump is primed and the suction line is free of air and blockage.

faults.name: Shaft misalignment
faults.reasoning: Misalignment between the pump and driver shafts loads the coupling and bearings and typically produces high vibration, often axial, sometimes with heat and noise.

triggers.symptom: Raised temperature at the bearings or coupling
Notes mention alignment, coupling or shaft problems

inspection_steps: Check pump-to-motor alignment with a dial gauge or laser alignment tool.
Check for soft foot and loose foundation or baseplate bolts.
Inspect the coupling for wear, cracks or overheated elements.
Check whether connected pipework is pulling on the casing (pipe strain).
maintenance_actions: Re-align pump and motor within the coupling manufacturer's tolerance.
Replace a worn coupling element.
Shim or re-grout the baseplate if uneven, and support the pipework properly.
safety: Lock out the driver before touching the coupling.
Re-fit the coupling guard before restarting.

faults.name: Impeller imbalance
faults.reasoning: Uneven mass on the rotating assembly (for example a fouled, eroded or damaged impeller) produces vibration at running speed that grows with speed.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention imbalance or impeller damage or fouling

inspection_steps: Inspect the impeller for fouling, erosion, cracks or missing material.
Check for a bent shaft or a loose impeller nut or key.
Measure vibration amplitude and see whether it is mainly at running speed.
Check whether the vibration changes with speed or flow.
maintenance_actions: Clean the impeller and remove deposits.
Replace or re-balance a damaged or eroded impeller.
Straighten or replace a bent shaft.
safety: Lock out the driver and drain the casing before opening the pump.
Handle the impeller carefully; worn edges can be sharp.

faults.name: Bearing wear
faults.reasoning: Worn or poorly lubricated bearings cause rising vibration, grinding or whining noise and heat at the bearing housing. Wear often develops gradually and is easily confused with misalignment.

triggers.symptom: High bearing housing temperature (70 °C or more)
Notes mention bearings, grease or grinding

inspection_steps: Measure bearing housing temperature and compare drive-end and non-drive-end.
Listen with a stethoscope or screwdriver for grinding or rumbling.
Check the lubricant level, condition and greasing history.
Check shaft end play and free rotation by hand, with the pump locked out.
maintenance_actions: Re-lubricate with the specified lubricant and quantity.
Replace worn bearings and check shaft and housing fits.
Find out why the bearing wore (misalignment, contamination, overloading) so it does not repeat.
safety: Lock out the driver before touching the shaft or coupling.
Allow hot bearing housings to cool before handling.

faults.name: Cavitation
faults.reasoning: When suction pressure is too low, vapour bubbles form and collapse inside the pump, causing a crackling or gravel-like noise, vibration, reduced flow and damage to the impeller over time. It depends on the suction conditions, so it only applies where those could be poor.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention suction problems, gravel noise or cavitation

inspection_steps: Check the suction line for blockage, a partly closed valve, a clogged strainer or air leaks.
Compare the available suction head (NPSH) with the pump's required value.
Check liquid temperature and suction level or tank level.
Check whether the noise changes when the discharge valve is opened slightly.
maintenance_actions: Clear or enlarge restrictions in the suction line and clean the strainer.
Raise the suction level or reduce suction losses, and keep the liquid cooler if possible.
Inspect the impeller for pitting and replace it if damaged.
safety: Do not run the pump dry while checking suction conditions.
Depressurise and drain before opening the suction line or strainer.

faults.name: Loose mounting / foundation
faults.reasoning: Loose baseplate bolts, a cracked grout bed or soft foot let the pump move under load, giving vibration and knocking or rattling noise.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention loose bolts, base or foundation problems

inspection_steps: Check all baseplate, foundation and casing bolts for tightness.
Look for cracked grout, rust marks or movement at the baseplate.
Check for soft foot at the pump and the motor.
Check whether the pipework supports are loose.
maintenance_actions: Tighten bolts to the specified torque.
Repair or replace damaged grout and re-level the baseplate.
Secure pipework supports.
safety: Lock out the driver before working on mounting bolts.
Support the pump safely if the baseplate is being loosened.

faults.name: Mechanical seal / packing leakage
faults.reasoning: A worn seal or packing leaks along the shaft; the cause is often dry running, misalignment, vibration or contamination.

triggers.symptom: Visible leakage at the seal or casing
Notes mention leakage or seal problems

inspection_steps: Find where the leak comes from: seal faces, gland packing, casing joint or a pipe connection.
Check seal flush or cooling lines and the condition of the packing.
Check shaft run-out and vibration, which shorten seal life.
Confirm the pump has not been running dry.
maintenance_actions: Replace the mechanical seal or adjust or replace the packing.
Correct any alignment, vibration or dry-running cause.
Re-tighten the gland evenly if it is packing, without over-tightening.
safety: Depressurise and drain the pump before opening the seal area.
Clean up leaks promptly to prevent slips, and wear gloves if the liquid is hot or hazardous.

faults.name: Impeller wear or blockage
faults.reasoning: A worn, eroded or partly blocked impeller reduces flow and pressure and can add noise and vibration.

triggers.symptom: Notes mention low flow, blockage or impeller wear

inspection_steps: Compare current flow, pressure and motor current with the pump curve.
Check the suction strainer and inlet for debris.
Inspect the impeller and wear rings for erosion, corrosion or clogging.
Check the internal clearances against the manufacturer's values.
maintenance_actions: Clear the blockage and clean the strainer.
Replace worn wear rings or the impeller.
Consider filtering the liquid if debris is a recurring problem.
safety: Lock out the driver and drain the casing before opening the pump.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling the impeller.
